title: Abstract thinkers and concrete thinkers
header_line: Jose's analysis of a book we are still naming. Not a summary of the book. Not affiliated with or endorsed by the author or publisher.

lines.text: Are you the one with the ideas or the one with the steps?
Jose said that there are two inclinations in business: creative, abstract, random thinkers, and the opposite, concrete, sequential ones.
A student said that a speaker used real, grounded words and not just big, abstract ideas.
Jose said that accountability language, whether from politicians or business leaders, comes down to the facts, concrete sequential information and deadlines.

A student said that if a salesperson has an outreach problem, you start with an audit of the data and give concrete answers: make fifteen more calls a day, or use these two lines in your script, then re-evaluate.
Jose said that you just described a strategy becoming operational, and that many businesses have people who are strategic with great ideas but cannot make it operational.
Another said that abstract thinkers tend to accomplish more than seems possible, and that a team and a board of different thinkers is needed. There will be productive friction.

exercise.title: Five minutes
steps: Write whether you are abstract or concrete.
Write who on your team is the other.
Write one idea as five concrete steps.
Write the data you will audit.

check.q: What did Jose call the two inclinations?
What did a student say you give for an outreach problem?
What did a student say a board of different thinkers brings?

recap: Pair the abstract with the concrete. Make strategy operational.
